title: Patch: a banned account leaves the ranked leaderboard, the percentiles and Jlorious
thread:
**Issue #3290 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #3290: Patch: a banned account leaves the ranked leaderboard, the percentiles and Jlorious
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the owner bans an account for cheating or abuse, it can no longer play. But its ranked standing stays on the public leaderboard for the rest of the season. It still counts toward the tier percentiles, and it keeps any place in Jlorious, the top group whose members earn the Jlorious card back. The honest player just below it is kept out.

Once this is built, a banned account's standing is left off the board and out of every count, as ladder bots already are. It comes back if the ban is lifted.

## Why

- `moderate ban` (`crates/server/src/cli/moderate.rs:69-87`, `crates/server/README.md:110-114`) sets `profiles.status` to banned (§9.1, `spec/09-architecture.md:46`), which refuses the account's next request.
- The standings read (`standings_from!`, `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs:5688-5703`) selects `p.kind` and the hand-set flag, but no status.
- `counts` and `listed` (`crates/shared/src/ranked/board.rs:68-108`) drop only ladder bots (R640000) and, on a strict server, hand-set ratings (R3074001).
- The leaderboard and Jlorious read those rows (`crates/server/src/api/ranked.rs`). The Jlorious card back goes to "the people this game leaves Jlorious" (`ranked.rs:208`, R2755000), so a banned row holding a top place changes who earns it.
- The spec says nothing about a banned account's standing. Hearthstone leaves banned accounts off its leaderboards.

## Proposal

- The standings read sets a server-side `banned` mark from `profiles.status`, in both stores. No client view of another player's standing carries it.
- `counts` and `listed` return false for a banned standing, as they do for a bot.
- Nothing is deleted, so lifting the ban restores the account's rows.
- A ruling in the issue's block, and one sentence in §9.12.

## Where it lands

- `crates/shared/src/ranked/board.rs` and `crates/shared/tests/board.rs`.
- `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`, `fake.rs` and `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`.
- `crates/server/tests/api/ranked.rs`.
- Spec §9.12, a new ruling note and `spec/pending/<issue>.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A shared test: a banned standing neither counts nor lists, and bots and hand-set ratings behave as before.
- [ ] An API test: after a ban, the leaderboard leaves the account out and the next account takes its Jlorious place. After an unban the account is back.
- [ ] A store contract case: the standings read carries the status on both stores.
- [ ] The ruling's proving test is named after it, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.

## Size and risks

Small to medium, about 8 files.

Risks:
- Jlorious is worked out when ratings are written, so a mid-season ban reshuffles it at the next ranked game. The ruling should say whether that is enough.
- A generated TypeScript type may gain a field. Keep the mark out of what the client reads about other players.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

## Goal

A banned account (`profiles.status = 'banned'`) leaves the public ranked leaderboard (its Grape tier row, its Jlorious place, the Raisin count), the tier percentiles and Jlorious, on every server, as a ladder bot already leaves the percentiles and Jlorious.   - After `status("active")` it reads `false` again.

  - New `mod r3290000_a_banned_account_leaves_the_board` with `use super::*;`, `use jackioh_server::cli::moderate::{ban_profile, unban_profile};`, `use jackioh_server::economy::store::EconomyReason;`, `use super::r2755000_the_jlorious_card_back::backs;`.
  - Add a helper `ids(listed: &Value) -> (Vec<String>, Vec<String>)`: the Jlorious ids, then every tier's player ids flattened.
  - `r3290000_a_ban_takes_an_account_off_the_leaderboard_and_an_unban_brings_it_back`.
    - Seed with `seed_placed` the accounts `m-000..=m-100` (`JLORIOUS_SIZE + 1`, Mythic, rating `2000.0 - i`) and `g-a` (Golden, `tier_bottom(3) + 4`). Add a `raisin` (seed profile and `put_rank(fresh_rank)`, as the test near line 625 does).
    - `let before = board(&app, "m-001").await;` asserts 100 Jlorious ids from `m-000` to `m-099`, `m-100` in the Mythic tier and `raisins == 1`.
    - Call `ban_profile(&app.db, id)` for `m-000`, `g-a` and `raisin`.
    - In `after`, Jlorious is `m-001..=m-100` at positions 1 to 100, with `m-001` marked `you`.
    - In `after`, none of the three ids is anywhere in `ids(&after)`, and `raisins == 0`.
    - In `after`, `own(&app, "m-100").await["rank"] == {tier: jlorious, position: 100}`, and `after.to_string()` does not contain `banned`.
    - Call `unban_profile` for all three, then `board(&app, "m-001").await == before`.
  - `r3290000_the_account_that_takes_a_banned_places_jlorious_gets_its_peak_and_card_back_at_the_next_rated_game`.
    - Same 101 Mythic accounts, plus `x` and `y` (`tier_bottom(1)`, 1000.0). Ban `m-000`.
    - `backs(&app, "m-100")` is empty and its `ranked_rank(..)` `peakJlorious` is null.
    - Call `rate(&app, game("g-1", [player("x"), player("y")], Some(0), 1))`.
    - Then `backs(&app, "m-100") == [(EconomyReason::Jlorious, Some("g-1".to_string()))]`, its `peakJlorious == 100`, and `m-000` has no card back and no peak.

- `cargo test -p jackioh-shared --test board r3290000`

## Done when

- [ ] `SeasonStanding.banned` exists; `counts` and `listed` are false for it; bots and hand-set ratings are unchanged (shared test).
- [ ] Both stores set `banned`; the contract case passes on the fake. The Postgres suite runs in CI's `db` job, not here.
- [ ] API tests: a ban removes the account and the next one takes its Jlorious place; an unban restores the board exactly.
- [ ] The R3290000 note, `spec/pending/3290.md` and the §9.12 sentence are in; `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] The generated TS diff is only `banned?: boolean` in two files.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh catalog check` and `cargo jackioh patches check` pass. Run `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` if `origin/main` is present.

## Risks

- **The wire types gain a field.** `banned` is `skip_serializing_if` false, like `bot` and `handSet`, so an old host's JSON still parses. No response body (`LeaderboardBody`, `SeatRank`, `VisibleRank`) holds a `SeasonStanding`, and the API test asserts the leaderboard body never says `banned`.
- **Purity and determinism.** Nothing impure or hash-ordered is added; `crates/shared` stays pure.
- **Stale Jlorious writes.** A mid-season ban leaves peaks and card backs as written until the next rated game on that ladder. Ruling (d) says so and the second API test proves it.
- **A banned person with no season row** playing a running game is treated as unbanned for that one game. A new row has no ladder position, so it cannot hold a Jlorious place, and every later read marks it.
- **Unban.** `profiles_set_status` from banned to active is already supported in both stores (the `moderate` tests use it).

## Open questions

None blocking. Decisions made that the task did not settle:
- The ban is read live at each read: no backfill at ban time and no revoking of an owned card back.
- The mark applies on every server, not only strict ones.
- `dev_leaderboard` still lists banned rows unchanged.
```

## Risks

- **The wire types gain a field.** `banned` is `skip_serializing_if` false, like `bot` and `handSet`, so an old host's JSON still parses. No response body (`LeaderboardBody`, `SeatRank`, `VisibleRank`) holds a `SeasonStanding`, and the API test asserts the leaderboard body never says `banned`.
- **Purity and determinism.** Nothing impure or hash-ordered is added; `crates/shared` stays pure.
- **Stale Jlorious writes.** A mid-season ban leaves peaks and card backs as written until the next rated game on that ladder. Ruling (d) says so and the second API test proves it.
- **A banned person with no season row** playing a running game is treated as unbanned for that one game. A new row has no ladder position, so it cannot hold a Jlorious place, and every later read marks it.
- **Unban.** `profiles_set_status` from banned to active is already supported in both stores (the `moderate` tests use it).

None blocking. Decisions made that the task did not settle:
- The ban is read live at each read: no backfill at ban time and no revoking of an owned card back.
- The mark applies on every server, not only strict ones.
- `dev_leaderboard` still lists banned rows unchanged.

    - Call `ban_profile(&app.db, id)` for `m-000`, `g-a` and `raisin`.
    - In `after`, Jlorious is `m-001..=m-100` at positions 1 to 100, with `m-001` marked `you`.
    - In `after`, none of the three ids is anywhere in `ids(&after)`, and `raisins == 0`.
    - In `after`, `own(&app, "m-100").await["rank"] == {tier: jlorious, position: 100}`, and `after.to_string()` does not contain `banned`.
    - Call `unban_profile` for all three, then `board(&app, "m-001").await == before`.
  - `r3290000_the_account_that_takes_a_banned_places_jlorious_gets_its_peak_and_card_back_at_the_next_rated_game`.
    - Same 101 Mythic accounts, plus `x` and `y` (`tier_bottom(1)`, 1000.0). Ban `m-000`.
    - `backs(&app, "m-100")` is empty and its `ranked_rank(..)` `peakJlorious` is null.
    - Call `rate(&app, game("g-1", [player("x"), player("y")], Some(0), 1))`.
    - Then `backs(&app, "m-100") == [(EconomyReason::Jlorious, Some("g-1".to_string()))]`, its `peakJlorious == 100`, and `m-000` has no card back and no peak.

Commands:
- `cargo test -p jackioh-shared --test board r3290000`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-shared --test ranked_game r3290000`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store r3290000`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server r3290000`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-shared --features ts`
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server`

## Done when

- [ ] `SeasonStanding.banned` exists; `counts` and `listed` are false for it; bots and hand-set ratings are unchanged (shared test).
- [ ] Both stores set `banned`; the contract case passes on the fake. The Postgres suite runs in CI's `db` job, not here.
- [ ] API tests: a ban removes the account and the next one takes its Jlorious place; an unban restores the board exactly.
- [ ] The R3290000 note, `spec/pending/3290.md` and the §9.12 sentence are in; `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] The generated TS diff is only `banned?: boolean` in two files.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh catalog check` and `cargo jackioh patches check` pass. Run `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` if `origin/main` is present.

## Risks

- **The wire types gain a field.** `banned` is `skip_serializing_if` false, like `bot` and `handSet`, so an old host's JSON still parses. No response body (`LeaderboardBody`, `SeatRank`, `VisibleRank`) holds a `SeasonStanding`, and the API test asserts the leaderboard body never says `banned`.
- **Purity and determinism.** Nothing impure or hash-ordered is added; `crates/shared` stays pure.
- **Stale Jlorious writes.** A mid-season ban leaves peaks and card backs as written until the next rated game on that ladder. Ruling (d) says so and the second API test proves it.
- **A banned person with no season row** playing a running game is treated as unbanned for that one game. A new row has no ladder position, so it cannot hold a Jlorious place, and every later read marks it.
- **Unban.** `profiles_set_status` from banned to active is already supported in both stores (the `moderate` tests use it).

## Open questions

None blocking. Decisions made that the task did not settle:
- The ban is read live at each read: no backfill at ban time and no revoking of an owned card back.
- The mark applies on every server, not only strict ones.
- `dev_leaderboard` still lists banned rows unchanged.
